text:
Rita - Support: FYI customer #32456 reporting huge p95/p99 regressions on text-generation endpoints since last night, looks like many requests are hitting 1-2s now (they expect <200ms). attaching support ticket and sample traces.

Sam O'Neill: oncall, I can take this. which model and region? any recent deploys?

Rita - Support: model=redwood-3-small, region=us-west-2, traffic pattern = bursty bursts from a single tenant (spike at ~03:10 UTC). No code deploys listed in changelog, but runtime config change went out yesterday at 22:30.

Ash K: I see a correlation on infra metrics — p50 stable, p95/p99 spiked. looks like batching tail behavior. paging runtime team.

Mike L: pinged. We recently increased continuous-batcher.batch_timeout_ms from 40 -> 200 to improve throughput on embeddings workload. suspecting tradeoff caused long waits for sparse traffic.

Eve - Eng ML: can we get a snippet of the current batching config and any batch flush logs?

Mike L: here's the config that rolled last night (from prod-configs):

```
continuous-batcher:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 64
  batch_timeout_ms: 200
  max_waiters: 8
  adaptive_scaling: false
```

Mike L: logs from the batcher show many batches waiting near timeout: `batch_wait_time_ms ~ 190` and then flush -> large per-request added latency. sample log entries:

```
[2025-11-02T22:58:12Z] batcher: created batch id=0x1f4 waiters=3 wait_time_ms=188
[2025-11-02T22:58:12Z] batcher: flushing batch id=0x1f4 size=3 reason=timeout
[2025-11-02T22:58:12Z] runtime: request latency breakdown: queue=190ms compute=15ms network=6ms
```

Ash K: that matches p99 spike. small batches in sparse traffic get held to hit throughput targets -> long queue latency. previous value 40ms kept tail low.

Rita - Support: customer is escalating because their SLAs were missed and billing tier was triggered due to longer request windows. they want root cause and mitigation plan ASAP.

Sam O'Neill: immediate mitigation options: a) rollback batch_timeout_ms to 40 across affected nodes, b) set per-tenant override to disable batching for that tenant, c) enable force_flush_on_request_size=true so small requests don't wait. Which is least risky?

Mike L: safest quick change is to roll batch_timeout_ms back to 40 in us-west-2 canary and observe. per-tenant override requires wiring into routing and is riskier. force_flush toggle is doable but needs a hotfix on runtime in case it interacts with caching.

Ash K: action plan: 1) canary rollback in us-west-2 on 10% of nodes now. 2) monitor p95/p99 and error rates for 10m. 3) if stable, full rollback and postmortem.

Sam O'Neill: executing canary rollback now. infra-bot, create canary change and patch config.

infra-bot: change_request created: CR-7891, patcher started on pool "rbw-prod-usw2-batcher" (10% nodes). tracking url: https://internal.redwood/config/CR-7891

Mike L: running quick metric queries: `rcli metrics query "latency_ms{model=\"redwood-3-small\",region=\"us-west-2\"}" --window 5m`

Eve - Eng ML: also adding a guard: adaptive_scaling=true should be turned on in future to tune timeouts based on traffic. For now, keep it off until we validate.

[~8 minutes later]

Sam O'Neill: canary shows p99 drop from ~1.9s -> ~180ms on the patched nodes. overall cluster p99 decreased by ~30% (still some noisy nodes).

Rita - Support: told customer we're rolling a rollback, ETA 20-30m for full rollout. they acknowledged :thumbsup:.

Mike L: proceeding with full rollback. disabling the 200ms change across all batcher pools in us-west-2.

infra-bot: change_request CR-7891 completed on 100% of targeted nodes.

Sam O'Neill: metrics now look good across region: p95 ~120ms, p99 ~240ms. error rate normal. closing escalation with customer.

Eve - Eng ML: follow-ups: - add canary threshold checks for batcher config changes (dont push >50ms without explicit approval) - implement per-tenant batching policies in routing layer - consider adaptive batching (auto-lower timeout when queue length low)

Ash K: scheduling a postmortem tomorrow 15:00 UTC. include runtime, ml, support, and product. assign owners for mitigations.

Rita - Support: adding notes to ticket #32456 and sending reimbursement offer per SLA.

Mike L: preliminary root cause: config change increased batch timeout to favor throughput on different workload; didn't account for long-tail effect on sparse, bursty tenants. regression not caught by canary because canary traffic was uniform and higher QPS.

Sam O'Neill: closing loop: patch to add `max_effective_batch_timeout_ms` per-tenant, and CI test that simulates bursty single-tenant traffic.

Rita - Support: thanks team. customer confirmed recovery and appreciated quick response. :relieved:

Ash K: postmortem link once written: https://wiki.redwood/postmortems/2025-11-batcher-timeout-p99

Mike L: also adding a runtime metric `batch_wait_histogram` and alert if >5% of requests see wait >100ms.

Eve - Eng ML: will draft PR for adaptive batcher and add unit/integration tests (repro harness included).

Sam O'Neill: nice job everyone. lesson: batching knobs move throughput <-> tail latency, must be tested for bursty/low-traffic patterns.

Rita - Support: closing thread, will update ticket after postmortem.
